Hi Alice — thanks for these great questions. Per our internal review, please find a short answers summary below and attached drafts (RTBF SOP + SLA). Happy to walk through details on our call Thu 3/11.

Short answers:
1) Primary datastore deletion: We perform a logical delete immediately upon receiving a verified RTBF request. Primary data (user records) are removed from the live store within 24 hours in typical cases; associated KV caches are invalidated immediately. Physical purge from replicas/compacted storage completes as background work and is typically finished within 72 hours for standard configurations.

2) Backups & snapshots:
- Standard hosted backups are immutable snapshots. By default snapshots are retained per our backup policy (snapshot lifecycle: 30 days before eligible for permanent deletion; archival copies kept up to 90 days).
- For enterprise customers we can: (a) provide a contractual SLA to shorten the snapshot retention window to 30 days for new snapshots, or (b) maintain a documented process to mark a customer for expedited purge on the next maintenance window.
- For legal holds, we will not purge data until the hold is lifted. We will surface the hold and assist with documented exceptions.

3) Geo-replicas: Deletion requests are applied to the canonical (primary) copy. Replicas follow the same lifecycle, but there may be a short replication window where data exists in other regions (typically minutes to a few hours). Snapshots/archival copies in other regions follow the snapshot lifecycle above.

4) Logs & analytics:
- Audit & request logs are retained 90 days by default. Logs may contain identifiers; we do not store full PII in analytics pipelines by default, and we offer redaction/export options on request.
- For customers needing shorter retention or stricter controls we can implement tokenization/redaction at ingestion for an additional configuration step.

5) Private/on-prem: Customers running Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) are responsible for their own snapshot/backup lifecycle unless they engage Redwood-managed backup add-on; in that case we can align to the same contractual SLA as hosted deployments.
